comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C29, C30. Both evaluations affirm the mouse model design and molecular characterization showing specific deletion of AS isoforms while maintaining canonical p53 expression. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C3-C6, C57-C59. Both evaluations strongly support the core finding of male-specific protective effect lost in mutant mice. Peer reviewers describe this as 'compelling demonstration' and OpenEval notes 'statistically significant sex-specific differences.' Complete concordance on central finding.

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C47. Both evaluations support the finding that standard p53 functional assays show no differences between WT and mutant cells. Peer reviewers explicitly cite this as strength establishing phenotype specificity, matching OpenEval's interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C48, C50-C52. Both evaluations support the spontaneous lymphoma data showing sex-specific differences. OpenEval notes small numbers introduce uncertainty about statistical power, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'subtle pathogenic phenotype' without expressing concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C75, C76, C80. Both evaluations support the B cell population findings as key mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly cite 'higher number of immature B cells' as important difference. OpenEval additionally addresses C81 (correlation with lymphoma speed) which peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate but implicitly accept.

Perfect agreement on claims C84-C86, C90-C91. Both evaluations support the RNA-seq findings of limited differentially expressed genes with Ackr4 and Mt2 as most significant. OpenEval notes borderline significance introduces minor uncertainty, while peer reviewers accept the limited gene set as part of the subtle phenotype without concern.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C94-C97. Both evaluations support the multiple lines of evidence establishing Ackr4 as a p53 transcriptional target (MEF data, ChIP-Atlas, luciferase assays). Peer reviewers describe evidence as convincing without methodological challenges, matching OpenEval's 'well-supported' assessment.

Strong agreement on claims C10, C101, C102, C114. Both evaluations support the estrogen regulation of Ackr4/ACKR4 transactivation. OpenEval addresses C115 implicitly while peer reviewers explicitly note estrogen repression. Both accept this as explaining sex-specific phenotype without questioning the mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C118, C123. Both evaluations support the male-specific prognostic value of ACKR4 in Burkitt lymphoma from patient datasets. OpenEval additionally addresses C121, C125 (specificity to Burkitt vs other malignancies), while peer reviewers focus on the positive Burkitt finding and treat it as strong translational evidence.

Perfect agreement on claims C13, C138. Both evaluations support the functional validation showing ACKR4 knockout increases migration without affecting proliferation. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting the proposed mechanism, matching OpenEval's assessment of 'mechanistic evidence for tumor suppressive function.'

Agreement on claim C111. Both evaluations support the GSEA finding of Myc target enrichment. OpenEval addresses C149-C150 (mechanistic interpretation) and notes the pathway remains 'partially speculative,' while peer reviewers accept the finding as supporting the mechanistic model without expressing reservations.

Partial agreement on claims C40, C67. Both evaluations acknowledge the mRNA-protein discrepancy data. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretation about p53-AS contribution to stability (C39, C41, C66) lacking direct mechanistic evidence, while peer reviewers accept the observation without challenging the interpretation.

Agreement on claims C119-C120. Both evaluations support the negative findings for MT2A in human datasets. OpenEval additionally addresses C124 (lack of correlation in other malignancies) and frames these as strengthening specificity of ACKR4 findings. Peer reviewers implicitly accept without explicit critique.

Partial overlap on claim C122. OpenEval addresses C116-C117, C122 regarding sex-specific ACKR4 expression patterns in top expressors. Peer reviewer R9 focuses on C118, C122-C123 regarding prognostic value. Both support the findings but emphasize different aspects of the human data analysis.

OpenEval addresses claims C63-C70 regarding negative results ruling out obvious mechanisms (DNA mutations, p53 expression in tumors, proliferation markers). These data are supported by OpenEval and establish pre-tumoral origin of phenotype. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though implicitly accepted as part of overall study.

OpenEval addresses claims C107-C110 regarding Myc binding at Mt2 promoter and regulation. Evaluation notes interpretation is speculative but reasonable given GSEA results. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers accept the Mt2 findings as part of the transcriptomic analysis.

OpenEval addresses claims C136-C137 regarding validation of ACKR4 knockout cell lines (DNA sequencing, proliferation assays). Evaluation supports the validation but notes limitation of using only two clones. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers accept the functional studies without methodological concerns.

OpenEval rates claims C82-C83, C141-C142 as UNCERTAIN regarding E-mu-Myc specificity and broader relevance to spontaneous lymphomas. Notes limited data with small numbers makes interpretation speculative. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found addressing this specific concern about generalizability.

OpenEval rates claims C145-C147 as UNCERTAIN regarding mechanistic interpretation of relative contributions of p53-alpha abundance versus p53-AS function. Notes model is plausible but requires additional experiments for definitive support. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found addressing this mechanistic uncertainty.

OpenEval rates claims C128, C139, C152-C153 as UNCERTAIN regarding proposed mechanistic models linking ACKR4 to MYC activity and B cell differentiation. Notes migration phenotype is clear but connections remain largely speculative. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval addresses claims C37-C38 regarding relative abundance of isoforms established by RT-qPCR and western blot. Notes technical limitation in separating protein bands may affect protein-level interpretations throughout study. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found addressing this technical concern.
